topic: Why per-stream decode speed flattens at low concurrency.
goal: Explain the flat zone of a concurrency sweep and the knee.
grill: I run a concurrency sweep on a decode endpoint.
Per-stream speed looks flat at first, then drops.
I do not trust my reading of the curve.

interjections.text: I didn't understand your question. It wasn't framed very well

facts.claim: Concurrency C is the number of live decode streams.
Iteration duration D is the time one decode step takes for the whole batch.
Per-stream speed is 1/D and stays flat while the batch shares one iteration; it drops only when the batch saturates compute.
facts.wrong: Per-stream speed drops immediately as C grows, because each stream waits for the others.
